faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52. For a standard full-time week of 38 hours, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual pay before tax and super. If you work different hours, adjust the weekly figure accordingly.

faqs.q: What is the casual loading and how does it affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% on top of the base hourly rate, as set by the Fair Work Commission. For example, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44/hour becomes $33.05/hour with casual loading. This compensates for entitlements like paid leave that casual employees don't receive. Use the checkbox on the timesheet to add casual loading to your base rate.

faqs.q: Does the calculator include superannuation and tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Super is estimated at 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid on top of your salary, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident rates with the full tax-free threshold and a 2% Medicare levy (using 2025–26 single reduction thresholds). HELP, Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not included. The result is an estimate only.

bodyMarkdown:
## How to Average a League Salary: From Hourly to Annual Pay

If you want to average a league salary – whether that’s the typical pay in your industry or a personal target – the first step is understanding how your hourly rate translates into annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures. This guide walks you through the conversion using a standard 38-hour week and a 52-week year, as recommended by the Fair Work Ombudsman and the Fair Work Commission.

### The Basic Formula

Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52.

For a full-time employee working 38 hours every week, the calculation is straightforward. For example, on the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour (from 1 July 2026), the annual gross pay is:

$26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,265.44

This figure assumes you work the same hours each week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. It’s a starting point for budgeting and comparing job offers.

### Weekly and Fortnightly Pay

To find your weekly pay, divide the annual figure by 52. For the example above, that’s $1,004.90 per week – matching the Fair Work Commission’s published rate. Your fortnightly pay is simply the weekly amount multiplied by two: $2,009.80. Many employers pay fortnightly, so this figure is useful for household budgeting.

### The National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage applies to employees not covered by an award or enterprise agreement. From 1 July 2026, it’s $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week. However, most employees are covered by an award that sets higher minimum rates. The Fair Work Ombudsman publishes [pay guides](/blog) for each award, listing minimum pay rates, allowances, and penalty rates. Always check the correct award for your industry and role.

Award rates can be significantly higher than the National Minimum Wage. For example, the average weekly earnings for full-time adult employees in May 2026 were $2,083.70, according to the Australian Bureau of Statistics. That equates to an hourly rate of about $54.83 for a 38-hour week. If you’re aiming to average a league salary, comparing your offer against industry benchmarks like these is essential.

### Casual Loading

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. This compensates for not receiving paid leave entitlements. On the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 × 1.25). The [timesheet](/) calculator includes a checkbox to add casual loading. **Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading** – the tool adds it for you.

### Superannuation and Tax

Superannuation is paid on top of your gross pay. The super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 (2026–27). For the National Minimum Wage example, super would be $6,271.85 per year ($52,265.44 × 0.12). This is not deducted from your pay; it’s an additional contribution by your employer.

Tax is calculated using the 2026–27 resident rates:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus a 2% Medicare levy (using 2025–26 single reduction thresholds). The [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool estimates your net pay after tax and Medicare. Remember, this is an estimate – it doesn’t include HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging.

### Using the Timesheet Calculator

The [timesheet](/) on this site lets you enter your base hourly rate and choose whether to add casual loading. It then shows your annual, weekly, fortnightly, and monthly gross pay, along with estimated tax, Medicare, and super. The calculator assumes a 38-hour week and 52 weeks per year. If your hours vary, adjust the weekly figure manually.

### Annualised Wages and Salaries

Some awards allow annualised wages – a fixed annual amount that covers minimum pay, penalties, overtime, allowances, and annual leave loading. The Fair Work Ombudsman explains that these arrangements must be reviewed every 12 months to ensure the employee receives at least what they would have under the award. If you’re offered an annualised wage, compare it to the hourly conversion to make sure it’s fair.

### Putting It All Together

To average a league salary, start with your hourly rate. Multiply by 38 (or your actual weekly hours) and then by 52. Add casual loading if applicable. Compare the result to award rates, industry averages, and the National Minimum Wage. Factor in super (paid on top) and tax (deducted from gross pay). Use the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page for current rates and the [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page for benchmarks.

Remember: this conversion is a guide. Your actual pay may differ due to overtime, penalties, allowances, or enterprise agreements. Always check your award or employment contract for the correct entitlements.
